question: to the Commission Maciej Wąsik (ECR) Subject:

On 13 March 2026, Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier announced the finalisation of a loan agreement with the Polish Government under the EU Security Action for Europe (SAFE) programme, with the aim of disbursing a 15% advance payment (around EUR 6.5-6.6 bn) as early as April 2026. This Commission statement came despite Polish President Karol Nawrocki vetoing, on 12 March 2026, the SAFE legislation that was to regulate national mechanisms for the management, control, audit and repayment of the loan. As a result of the veto, that legislation did not enter into force. Polish constitutional experts and lawyers argue that taking on this SAFE borrowing in spite of the veto would constitute a significant infringement of the applicable Treaty provisions and therefore a breach of the rule of law. In light of the above: 1.

On what legal basis (specific articles of the SAFE Regulation and the Treaties) does the Commission intend to conclude an agreement and disburse funds without a national law implementing the management and repayment mechanisms?
Does the Commission consider that continuing the procedure without national legislation is not an infringement of Article 4(3) TEU (principle of sincere cooperation) or the rule of law?
Is the Commission aware of the consequences of making SAFE funds available contrary to a decision by the Polish authorities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.5.2026) Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106 of 27 May 2025 establishing the Security Action for Europe (SAFE)1 is based on Article 122 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union2 which provides a legal basis for the EU to act swiftly in emergency situations. The SAFE Regulation and in particular Article 10, explicitly empowers the Commission to enter into loan agreements and operational arrangements with Member States, following the adoption of a Council implementing decision. This Regulation does not condition disbursement on the prior adoption of a specific national implementing legislation by the Member State since the instrument is directly applicable. Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/412 on making the financial assistance under Regulation (EU) 2025/1106 available to Poland3 fulfils the procedural requirement under Article 10(1) of the Regulation4, and the Commission’s role is to ensure compliance with the eligibility criteria set out in Article 16 of the Regulation5. To date, Polish authorities have not raised any objections regarding the availability or disbursement of SAFE funds. The Commission will act in accordance with the Treaty and the SAFE Regulation, ensuring that all procedural safeguards are respected.

1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/1106/oj/eng. 2 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/treaty/tfeu_2016/art_122/oj/eng. 3 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dec_impl/2026/412/oj/eng. 4 Please see footnote 1. 5 Please see footnote 1.
